headline: Nasdaq-100 retraces about 115 points off a 29,040.25 session low after soft ISM and JOLTS prints, with VIX and the 10-year both easing from session highs
body:
The defining change this hour is that the down-leg finally produced a retracement. Nasdaq-100 futures extended the session low once more to 29,040.25 around the 14:00 UTC data block, but two independent quotes place them at 29,154.00-29,156.00 shortly after 14:18 UTC, roughly 115 points above that low. The cash Nasdaq-100 was 29,112.88 at 14:28 UTC, near the top of a 28,992.25-29,128.99 session range rather than pinned to the bottom of it. Across the previous three clock-hours the pattern was repeated extension with price sitting within a handful of points of each new low; that specific pattern is what the Tail definition targets, and it has now been interrupted.

The data were modest misses rather than shocks. ISM Manufacturing printed 54.6 for August against 55.2 expected and 55.6 in July, an eighth consecutive month of expansion, with New Orders down to 53.7 from 56.7, Employment 51.2 from 52.8, and the Prices sub-index unchanged at 71.1. JOLTS job openings for July came in at 7.271 million against 7.300 million expected, described by the Bureau of Labor Statistics as little changed at 7.3 million. Softer growth with unchanged price pressure is a mildly negative mix, but the release did not produce a disorderly repricing.

Cross-assets are stabilising at stressed levels. The 10-year Treasury yield is 4.764% after touching 4.790%, its highest intraday level since January 2025, and the 30-year remains near multi-decade highs around 5.27%. VIX is 15.66, up about 5%, but off a 16.06 session high. WTI is $87.62 and Brent $92.12, both firm after projectile strikes on two crude tankers exiting the Strait of Hormuz on Monday evening, yet neither is extending. Semiconductors remain the index transmission point, with Nvidia, AMD and Micron each near -2%.

Under the risk definitions in force, event importance and surprise magnitude are scored through Stress and Confidence, while Tail requires observed persistent one-way structure. That structure has now been broken by a pullback that has held for roughly twenty-five minutes with the index near its session high, so Tail moves from 31% to 24% and the mapped policy state moves from BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES to WATCH. Stress stays high at 71% because a 1.2% index decline, multi-decade-high long yields, firm crude and an unresolved geopolitical transit risk are all still present. Confidence is 88% on current verified levels, verified release actuals, current yields, VIX, crude and the seven-day calendar.

The shared Finviz cross-asset context was read at the start of the run but its collection timestamp of 10:50 UTC makes it roughly 220 minutes old, beyond the 90-minute freshness bound, so it was treated as stale and not used as evidence. The assessment rests entirely on independently fetched current sources.
lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment. The first eighteen, spanning the 31 August US session and the overnight hours, mapped to the EA_ON band with Tail between 9 and 13 and mode mixed, while Stress drifted from 53 up to 58 as crude firmed and long yields climbed. The regime changed from 08:00 UTC on 1 September, when Tail moved to 22 with mode trend-down and the overnight band gave way, then to 26 at 09:00 UTC for the first BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES reading of the sequence. Tail held at 25 through the 10:00 and 11:00 UTC hours on a 29,178 base, rose to 28 at 12:00 UTC when that base broke, and reached 31 at 13:00 UTC after a third consecutive hourly extension into the cash open. Stress rose in step from 65 to 75 and confidence stayed between 84 and 88 throughout.
outlookSummary: The base case over the next 24 hours is that the 1 September rates, crude and geopolitical repricing continues to resolve into two-sided trade. The projection starts from an observed retracement rather than from an extension, so Tail begins at 24 for the current 14:00 UTC hour and steps down through 22, 21 and 20 across the New York morning and early afternoon on the condition that the 29,040.25 low holds and volatility keeps decaying. A one-step lift to 21 at 18:00 UTC and a local peak of 24 with Stress 68 at 19:00 UTC carry the power-hour continuation and reversal checkpoint, which is treated as a scheduled structural risk rather than an observed path. From the 20:00 UTC cash close Tail falls to 20 and then into the EA_ON band overnight, bottoming at 12 through the Asian hours as ranges compress, before rising gradually to 15 across the European morning. The final two slots carry conditional checkpoints on 2 September: 18 at 12:00 UTC for the ADP employment print at 12:15 UTC and 20 at 13:00 UTC for the US cash open. No forecast hour reaches the blocking threshold, because a scheduled event is a checkpoint rather than observed one-way structure. Confidence decays from 88 to 63 with distance from the evidence cutoff.
